title: The Science of Falling in Love

blanks.sentence: The body sends _____ into the blood; these help control mood and are involved in falling in love.
blanks.section: NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS — Looking beyond romance

blanks.sentence: For some people who are _____, lust may not occur at all.
When it does occur, two hormones that drive it are _____.
Lust can encourage _____ by creating the urge to have offspring.
A rewarding feeling can encourage the _____ of a behaviour.

multipleChoice.question: How does the discussion initially shift from romantic expressions about love?
options: It examines how romantic language shapes people's expectations of a partner.
It compares the health effects of love with those of other emotions.
It considers chemical activity in the brain and body during love.
It explains why physical attraction usually develops before romance.

multipleChoice.question: Which qualification does the expert make about lust's place in romantic love?
options: It may appear first, but its timing and occurrence vary between people.
It usually follows attraction, though its intensity varies between people.
It develops in everyone, but some people notice it much later.
It appears first only when both people want to have children.

multipleChoice.question: What is the expert's contrast between how lust may feel and what it may serve?
options: It may feel rewarding, while encouraging a person to repeat a behaviour.
It may feel romantic, while helping a person choose a long-term partner.
It may feel stressful, while helping a person form an emotional bond.
It may feel purely physical, while supporting reproduction.

multipleChoice.question: What difficulty does the example of chasing new relationships suggest for some people?
options: They may struggle to feel rewarded by any romantic relationship.
They may struggle to stop seeking novelty in successive relationships.
They may form relationships mainly to reduce physical stress.
They may confuse physical desire with a wish to have children.
